The leg I am being asked to reconsider is three sessions old (filled 2026-09-16) and it was built for exactly the regime that has since been confirmed, so trading again now would be churn dressed up as work. What I checked before deciding: the FOMC did raise the target range 25bp to 3.75-4.00% on 9/16 - unanimous 12-0, first hike since 2023, explicitly justified by elevated inflation, with the median year-end funds rate marked up to 4.1%. The long end sold off with it rather than rallying: the 10y closed 5.01% on 9/18 against 4.79% at the start of September, with 2s at 4.10%, so the curve bear-steepened roughly 90bp while the Fed was tightening. That is a hot-nominal-growth, rising-discount-rate world, and it is the precise argument for owning high-ROIC net-cash franchises whose earnings reprice with nominal spend and who EARN the 4-5% on their own balance sheets instead of paying it. It is an argument against levered, long-payback, cash-burning duration. My five legs are the first thing and own none of the second.

Leg by leg, nothing broke. NVDA marks +3.91% at 222.27 on a 28x trailing multiple with Huang guiding to roughly double the chips shipped next year - that is a growth-adjusted multiple below the index's 25x, not a bubble leg. TSM marks +4.06% at 434.67 after a record NT$514.8bn August and with 2nm entering phones; it is the toll booth rather than the bet on any single accelerator winner, which is why it sits alongside NVDA rather than being crowded out by it. GOOGL, my largest weight at 24%, marks +1.95% and got the single best piece of news in the window: the unsealed adtech remedy is interoperability and publisher data sharing, not divestiture, which removes the tail risk that was the main reason to underweight it - and it still trades at 17.5x with revenue +20%. META marks -1.12% and is the cheapest thing I own at 20.6x forward while still -14% YTD; Muse topping the App Store and the Stilla.ai agent deal are early evidence the capex is starting to produce monetizable product, and I am not selling a laggard into the first sign the thesis is turning. V marks -0.71%, which is what ballast is supposed to do in a three-day window - it is my only non-AI leg and its whole job is to convert elevated inflation into fee revenue.

The one honest criticism of this book is concentration: 68% of gross sits in a single AI-complex factor, and if capex sentiment cracks four of my five legs fall together. I have decided to keep that exposure rather than diversify it away, because the 16% cash buffer plus stops at -14% to -20% and take-profits on the two hottest legs already define my loss, and because diluting into lower-ROIC non-tech compounders purely for correlation cosmetics would violate the mandate that picked these names in the first place. Re-trading would also reset every stop to a new, higher entry basis and silently loosen my downside - a real cost on top of the 4-8bp of commission and SEC fees a full replacement burns. NAV is +4.83% against SPY +2.73% on 84% gross; the position is working, the reason it was working has just been confirmed by the Fed and the tape, and the correct action when your thesis is confirmed is to let it run, not to trade on top of it.
